title: Your Codebase Knows More Than Your Documentation Does
description: Why documentation drifts away from production code—and how connected engineering context can close the gap.
body:
## The gap between documentation and reality
Architecture diagrams, technical specifications and onboarding guides describe a system at a moment in time. Software rarely stands still. Services change, dependencies grow, and business rules move while documentation struggles to keep up.

A new engineer may find the correct file in minutes and still spend days understanding why the code behaves as it does. Finding a function is not the same as understanding its purpose, dependencies, and constraints.

## Why static documentation falls behind
Documentation and implementation often live in separate workflows. A pull request can change behavior without updating a diagram. A new integration may not appear in the onboarding guide. The gap grows incrementally, until the team trusts conversations more than written material.

This creates friction in onboarding, incident response, modernization, and change reviews. It also concentrates knowledge in a few experienced engineers.

## Codebase understanding is a relationship problem
The useful questions cross artifact boundaries. Which requirement led to this behavior? Which services depend on it? Which tests protect it? What documentation will become outdated if we change it?

Search can find files and symbols. Answering those questions requires context that connects requirements, architecture, documentation and code.

## What changes with AI-assisted engineering
AI tools can help write code quickly, but speed alone does not establish system-level correctness. An assistant working without reliable context may overlook downstream effects or architectural constraints.

Teams need a dependable way to expose the context behind an implementation, not just the implementation itself.

## Toward connected engineering knowledge
A more sustainable model treats engineering knowledge as relationships that can be explored and reviewed as the system evolves. That can make impact analysis clearer, reduce repeated discovery work and help newcomers understand unfamiliar systems.

Interfluent is exploring this connected-context approach: bringing codebase understanding closer to the decisions engineers make every day.

## The practical starting point
Start with one critical workflow. Map its requirements, owning components, dependencies, and supporting documentation. Identify what is currently maintained by memory alone. Then make the connections reviewable whenever the workflow changes.

The goal is not more documentation. It is documentation people can actually trust.
